findings.issue: reviewHeader now returns { summary, shown } and is spread into ReviewPanel; the shown list is not part of the header, so the name undersells what it returns.
findings.fix: Rename to reviewPanelData (or similar), or pass summary/shown as explicit props from one completedHand(table) call as the spec sketch shows.

findings.issue: `.review-shown .table-cards { gap: 4px }` is not in the spec's CSS list.
findings.evidence: Spec 5 lists only .review-shown, .review-shown li and .review-shown svg[data-card].
findings.fix: Keep it if it's needed for the small cards (it's harmless); otherwise drop it.

findings.issue: The live test doesn't check whether pinned hand 1 reaches a showdown with an opponent showing. If it doesn't, the row equality check passes trivially on []. SPEC-08 allows either outcome, and the scene tests cover the showing case.
findings.fix: Optional: note in a comment which outcome the pinned words produce, or assert it.

summary: The implementation matches the spec. shownOpponents reads only CompletedHand.shown, leaves out the user's seat, copies the cards and throws the specified RangeError. The panel list sits between .review-head and the Decisions list, uses the spec's own hooks and avoids the locked ones. Copy matches Q-1 ('Ben showed' + drawn cards + ' · Pair of kings'). The hidden-card tests would catch a leak: they search for mucked (Dee 5c 5d) and folded (Ava/Cal/Eli; all five fold-out opponents) cards in the stripped text, aria-label/title/alt values, <title> text, data-card values and whole-word codes. The data-card allow-list is exact. The deep walk of the props covers every card-bearing key (only board and holeCards exist in review types) and bans the deck/players/burned keys. The tests also confirm each fixture's dealt cards, so the searches aren't vacuous. The variant and null shown cases plus a source grep cover the replay-code ban. The browser tests repeat the search, including an all-52-card label check in the live hand. Recorded deviation: the SPEC-04 search leaves out the user's seat as well as the shown seats. That's correct, because the header must show the user's own cards; accepted. The new unit and acceptance tests pass locally (7/7), and gate fix-2 is PASS. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
